_readme: Each value carries its measured basis. A ceiling is never set above what would stay green on the measured
failure state, and never below 0.7 x that measurement. Re-measure with `node tooling/ops/check-renovate-backlog.mjs --json`.

measured.source: #417 body and its userContentEdits (26 revisions, 2026-09-03T05:42:42Z to 2026-09-22T06:01:55Z)

majors.source: renovate.json packageRules: the approval rule's description ("the ten majors on #417", the drain triage of 2026-09-26) and the java-majors rule's (chore/renovate-java-25.x, "24.1 days waited on 2026-09-27")

maxWaiting.basis: 0.7 x the 21 waiting on 2026-09-22 = 14.7, rounded up. With prHourlyLimit 6 x two runs per Monday window = 12 PRs a week against 4.4 arriving, the queue before a Monday should hold about one week of arrivals; 15 is reached only after about two Mondays that opened nothing.

maxOldestDays.basis: An update found just after a Monday window waits up to 7 days for the next one; 14 is one whole missed Monday. 0.7 x the 19.0 days the oldest entry had waited on 2026-09-22 = 13.3, so 14 is above that bound and still red on the measured state.

maxWaitingMajors.basis: 0.7 x the 10 majors waiting for approval on #417 on 2026-09-27 = 7.0. Every major waits for a person (renovate.json dependencyDashboardApproval on majors), so no Monday window drains one, and ten majors beside three patches is 13 <= maxWaiting 15 and green. It must stay below maxWaiting, or the queue's ceiling would always fire first and this one never (readFloor refuses that).

maxOldestMajorDays.basis: The age ceiling a major is held to IN PLACE of maxOldestDays, and held EQUAL to it: before the split every major was aged against 14, and splitting majors out must not loosen that (readFloor refuses a value above maxOldestDays). It is below 0.7 x the 24.1 days chore/renovate-java-25.x had waited on 2026-09-27 (16.9) for that reason alone, and red on that state. An approved major opens in the next Monday window, so 14 is still one whole missed Monday after the approval.
